newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda reports brisk coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Uganda reports brisk coffee sales.

text.p: February started with promising results in Uganda's coffee trade with 348,046 60-kg bags registered for sale in the week ended February 7, compared with 22,098 in the previous week, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said in a report on Wednesday.
Robusta Screen 15 (standard) coffee grade dominated the market with some 145,502 bags. Screen 12 and and Screen 18 contributed 52,612 and 41,497, respectively.
Arabica drugar accounted for 10,000 bags, UCDA said but did not provide a breakdown for prices in the comparative week.

Local prices ranged between 1,150 shillings and 1,250 shillings for a kg of FAQ (Fair Average Quality). Kiboko prices were between 500 and 650 shillings a kg while arabica parchment moved between 1,350 and 1,450, UCDA said.
UCDA said the February outlook was bullish following reports that stocks in consuming countries were reported to have reached levels of 7.4 million bags.
UCDA added that Brazil might have a smaller crop of around 18-20 million bags in 1997/98 compared with 27 million in 1996/97.
Brazilian local consumption was projected at 12-13 million bags in 1997/98.
UCDA cited recent strikes and guerilla activities in Colombia as other factors supporting a bullish market.
Holidays in Vietnam had created a supply squeeze in the London robusta market.
